question: Which authentic MASM version and options produced the reviewed GAME_ASM routines in segment 4 (_TEXT)?
reason: The supplied executable and MAPSYM data preserve linked bytes and loader relocations, not the original assembler OMF records.

A synthetic unmarked forward-jump probe separates MASM 5.x from the tested MASM 6.x tools, but the corresponding EB displacement followed by 90h signature occurs zero times in the 32 reviewed GAME_ASM extents.

All seven authentic assemblers can independently produce the same strict _exchange complete member from readable source, so that member does not discriminate versions. Explicit SHORT qualifiers and source-level layout can also remove the probe distinction.

probe.shape: mov ax,1; unmarked forward JMP; explicit NOP; forward label; RET
probe.result_interpretation: The 5.x tools preserve the original forward-jump span with EB 02 90 followed by the explicit 90. The tested 6.x tools shorten the jump and emit only the explicit 90.

runners.masm611: DOSBox-X with the provisioned Windows 3.1 runtime for its DOS extender
runners.masm614: Native Windows x86 execution; this update is a Win32 ML executable, not a DOS executable

original_byte_scan.signature: EB xx 90 where xx is a positive signed short displacement
original_byte_scan.interpretation: This signature is present elsewhere in _TEXT, but none of its occurrences falls in a reviewed GAME_ASM extent; it cannot identify the assembler used for those routines.

strict_member_proof.cross_version_observation: The same readable member source was also a strict complete-member match with MASM 5.1, 5.1A, 6.0, 6.0B, 6.11, and 6.14. MASM 5.x used /MX to preserve the lowercase public name; the tested 6.x commands used no additional flags.

scope_limit: No historical source object or assembler command record was supplied. The evidence supports a proven assembler lane and a bounded version-family discriminator, not a unique historical version/options claim.
